en: Short-hafted and head-heavy. Opens shields, doors, and the occasional wall. Slow enough to get you killed.
Reaches further than anything else you own, and is useless the moment a corridor narrows.
A working blade, not a warrior's. Quick, light, and honest about what it cannot do.
A seeress's iron staff, caged at the head. It was made to be held on a high seat; it strikes like the iron rod it is.
Slower than a seax and hooked at the heel. Throw it and it lands as a blow, and then it is on the floor over there, ringing, and your hand is empty.
Riveted rings on a leather shirt. Turns an edge, and rings like a dropped purse when you run.
Gold leaf over lead, and thin enough to read the lead through. It catches the light like the real thing, which was the whole of the idea.
Struck by a mint that no longer exists, for a king nobody remembers. She remembers.
Uncut, unset, and weighs nothing at all. It catches every light in the dark, including the ones looking for it.
Neck-ring of twisted gold. Worn by someone who wanted to be seen, and buried by someone who agreed.
A slab of offering-gold the size of a shield. Carrying it is a decision you make once and regret continuously.
Dull, rust-flecked, and worth almost nothing to her. The forge disagrees.
Reforged by a smith who knew what it would be used for. She wants it badly — which is the problem, because so do you.
Grey, unremarkable, and the only thing down here that is worth more than what you came for. Spending it ends the run with whatever is in your hands.
A piece of her fire, going out. It is heavier than it has any right to be and it will not stop making noise, and it is someone you know.
Linden boards under a rawhide rim. A blade held up takes nothing off a hammer coming down or a stone in the air; this does. It wants the hand the lantern wants.
Iron bands riveted over a leather cap. A hammer that finds your head still hurts; it does not leave you deaf and swaying for the better part of a minute.
Two curved plates laced over the forearms. Put an arm up against a falling blow and it stays an arm — your guard and your two-hander survive the hit.
Scraped horn instead of glass, because glass does not survive being carried. Shutter it and the dark comes back; leave it open and everything down here knows where to look.
A strip of boiled linen and the time to tie it. Four seconds with your hands busy, and a blow or a run undoes the knot.
A stave cut with a single rune. Break it and nothing near you makes a sound — until the wood gives out, and everything hears it go.
Shield-sworn. The last one standing in a doorway, and the one who decides where the doorway is.
Gets out by refusing to be stopped — heavy, armoured, and still moving under weight that would pin anyone else. Loud. The Hunt finds them easily.
Quieter than a blade and slower to bring to bear. What it buys you is that nothing has to know where you were standing.
The professional who was never seen. Knows which way you came, how long ago, and where the ground gives you away.
Gets out by never having been noticed — a bow, a trap, and a route chosen before anything looked up. Poor in a straight fight. Cornered is usually dead.
Wolf-coat. Goes without mail and does not step back. The thing in the dark that the dark should be afraid of.
Gets out through whatever is in the way — a fury that cannot be ended, blood that is paid when it is over, and a body weaker than its wont until it passes.
Seeress. Sits where others run, and comes back knowing where the thing in the dark was standing.

Gets out by leaving before it goes wrong — a trance sat still while the Hunt walks, and a reading of the Gold-Sick, the best of the floor and the way out, true for the moment it was taken. Frail. Helpless while she sees.
Seiðr: hold to sit in a trance — still, guard down — and the party sees where the Gold-Sick, the best find and the way out were
The ward-songs hold the trance through one blow. The blow still lands.
A reading also marks every awake enemy within twenty paces, where it stood.
A reading also marks where the Gold-Sick is going.
Where you sat stays hushed a while after a reading, and cracks loud as a rune when it breaks.
What you set down lands at your feet, instead of skidding away into the dark.
Gold knows your hands. Taking or setting down anything gilt makes no sound at all.
You know what a thing is worth to her before you decide whether to carry it.
A drop under a full load lands quiet. The weight is still there; the noise is not.
You can take what is at your feet without closing your bag first.
Raw stock and scrap weigh nothing to you. It is not treasure; it is ballast you can sell.
No load is heavy enough to keep you off a ledge. It will still slow you and it will still be heard.
Your bag shuts the instant you let go of it.
Weight makes you slow. It no longer makes you loud.
Nothing you take, set down or rummage for makes a sound.
The Gullsjúkr stops singling you out for being the richest thing in the room. It can still hear you.
There is no limit to what you can carry. Every kilogram of it makes you slower and louder than it would make anyone else. You can haul the whole vault out. The Deep will hear you do it.
You know what gold is worth to her. Anything you set down is worth her stooping for — and she will take it.
Soft hide, and it makes no sound at all. Room for more than your hands will hold, and not for a hoard.
Ash staves lashed with rawhide, and room for a hoard on your back. It creaks under the load, walking or standing still.
A Dvergar king's coin, still in the king's chest. You can lift it. You cannot lift it quietly, and you will not be running anywhere.
The otter-skin the first hoard was paid over, and never quite covered. Wear it and the Gold-Sick cannot feel what you carry. She would give almost anything to have it back.
Bleeding out — %d s. Your ember will drop where you fall.
A hand on you. Hold still.
Vörðr. You are loose, and nothing can touch you. Scout for them.
Vörðr. Your ember is on the floor, and nobody is left standing.
%s — get back up. You have one, and it is gone for the rest of the run.
Your one way up is spent. Hold on, or go out.
On {where} there is one thing worth more than the rest, and something sitting on it. Bring it up with you when you come out. We'd like to know the Deep still gives things back.
There's a {target} on {where}. It has cost us two crews. We'd sleep better if it stayed down.
One of ours built a cairn in the deepest room on {where} and didn't come back to say which way it lies. Find it and stand by it a moment. That's all we ask.
She wants three gilded torcs. When she has them, she will open more of herself to you.
Three torcs. She is pleased, and the deepest of her gifts are yours to buy.
She wants four coins of the old mint. When she has them, she will open more of herself to you.
Four coins. She is pleased, and the deepest of her gifts are yours to buy.
She wants three uncut stones. When she has them, she will open more of herself to you.
Three stones. She is pleased, and the deepest of her gifts are yours to buy.
She wants an altar-plate, from the bottom of the Delvings. When she has it, she will open more of herself to you.
The altar-plate. She is pleased, and the deepest of her gifts are yours to buy.
A Waystone, for your next descent
Two bindings, for your next descent
The plans: where each floor's Prize and Shaft lie
Your ember is down there, and everything you were carrying is with it. The hoard is untouched — it always is. She is waiting at the fire.
No descent returns nothing. This lineage carries %d lessons out of the Deep — where things were, what they did, and who would speak to you.
No descent returns nothing. This lineage carries its first lesson out of the Deep — where something was, what it did, or who would speak to you.
Nothing yet. What she will not let one life keep — tribute past what its rank can hold — is what a lineage learns, and this one has not given her that much.
That life was a %s, at rank %d. It is over.
A thing you wore or set aside, or a lesson you bought. Never Boon — she does not deal in measures. What she keeps comes back Scarred: weaker than it was, and worth nothing to her.
You found the surface once. She noticed.
%s's ember, carried the whole way. It was heavy and it was loud and you did it anyway.
You went down, you came back, and you took nothing. She does not understand it either.
The best thing down there is still down there.
There was almost nothing left of you at the door.
That is what you owed. You owe me nothing more this cycle.
More than you owed. Ask something of me.
Bring it to my pile (%s). What you owe me first; past that, I pay in boon.
You hold %d boon. Ask it of me at my pile (%s).
Boon is what she pays for tribute past the Tithe — %d of %d toward the next.
Crouching stops being quiet-ish and starts being silent.
An empty bag costs you nothing to run with. Come down light and you can run all day.
A sprint is no louder than a walk. Whatever is listening learns nothing from your hurry.
What you carry stops announcing itself. The weight is still there; the sound of it is not.
Stop moving and eyes slide off you. Ears do not — hold your breath as well.
Standing still gives your breath back, however much you are carrying.
Rummage at a walk. It is still both hands, and it is no longer both feet.
A Waystone takes you almost before you have finished asking.
A friend's ember stops weighing what a friend weighs. It is still as loud as it ever was.
Take a wound and you may be three seconds ago instead — once a floor. The ground you left roars where you were standing, and everything hears which room the fight was in.
A Waystone takes you without a sound. Whatever was coming arrives to an empty room.
A Shaft opens for you faster than it opens for anyone. It is still closing while you work.
You can get a friend up without telling the floor you are doing it.
While you Hold, your raised shield stops blows from the sides as well as the front. You still cannot move.
Letting go of a Hold throws everything in front of you back a step and staggers it. It is loud, and it takes your breath.
While you Hold, a blow aimed at a friend standing behind you lands on you instead.
You can keep holding with no breath left. Every moment you hold past empty costs you blood, and it does not come back down here.
Your snare makes a small footstep every few seconds until something steps in. It calls anything — the Gold-Sick too.
Each kill in the fury strikes something from the blood it owes.
The howl that opens your fury staggers everything near you, as a blow would.
Each blow you land in the fury feeds it a second, up to its length again.
A heavy blow in the fury leaves no wound. Its blood is still owed.
Scree under your feet is only stone: no louder than any other ground.
Choke-damp no longer holds your breath. It still holds everyone else's.
Your lamp burns in choke-damp, and opens in it.
Breath returns while your guard is up.
A blow to the head does not ring it. No concussion.
A broken arm still guards, and still holds a two-handed weapon. It is still broken.
Neither a blow nor a sprint undoes a binding you are tying.
A wound you already carry as a Scar is not taken again. The healed place holds.
A blade held up turns a heavy blow, as a shield does. Not a stone or an arrow.
A gashed leg does not slow you. The limp is still heard.
Standing still, your guard covers your back as well as your front.
The Deep's grounds do not touch you — scree, choke-damp, any of them. You cannot sprint.
Whatever your snare holds cannot call its kin while it is held.
An arrow into something that has not noticed you pins it where it stands, as your snare would. Loosing one springs any snare you have set.
For a few seconds after your snare fires, you make no sound at all.
glitter — hers, if you give it
the fury will not go %s until it has run out
the fury will not let you leave until it has run out
Hold: plant yourself and nothing gets past — breath drains while you stand
Snare: kneel to set a trap at your feet — silent to set, loud when it shuts
Wolf-Fury: hold to howl — blows are owed, paid when it ends; no step back, no bag
